'''Tsushima no Taue Odori''' (津島の田植踊) is a traditional folk performance of rice planting dance from {{ill|Tsunami, Namie, Fukushima|ja|福島県双葉郡浪江町津島|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunami, Namie, Fukushima|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Japan. It is recognized as a {{ill|Intangible Folk Cultural Properties Requiring Documentation|lt=Intangible Folk Cultural Properties Requiring Documentation|lt=Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|選択無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 記録作成等の措置を講ずべき無形の民俗文化財}} by the national government and as a prefectural {{ill|Folk Cultural Property|ja|無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 民俗文化財|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24895900}} of Fukushima Prefecture.

This rice planting dance is a form of {{ill|Yoshuku|lt=Yoshuku|lt=Yoshuku performing arts|ja|予祝芸能|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshuku performing arts|qq=}} that prays for abundant harvests, passed down through four villages in Namie: Kamitsushima, Shimotsushima, Minamitsushima, and Akugun. It was traditionally performed on {{ill|January 14 (Lunisolar)|ja|1月14日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/January 14th (lunar calendar)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q839082}}, {{ill|January 15 (Lunisolar)|ja|1月15日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/January 15th (lunar calendar)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q838395}}, and {{ill|January 17 (Lunisolar)|ja|1月17日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/January 17th (lunar calendar)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q838983}} but is now conducted according to the Gregorian calendar. On the first day, January 14th, the dance is dedicated at each village's respective {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shrine}}, followed by performances at houses upon request.

The performance features distinct roles:
* '''Kuwagashira''' (鍬頭): The leader who wears a {{ill|Zhongyi|ja|長襦袢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagajuban|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 襦袢|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55358825}}, secures a brocade sash (緞子), twists a {{ill|Tenugui|en|Tenugui|qid=Q2403941|lt=Tenugui}} around their head, and carries a large calabash.
* '''Taneoroshi''' (種下ろし): Two performers in {{ill|montsuki-haori-hakama|ja|紋付羽織袴|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mon-tsuki haori hakama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11605315}}, equipped with short swords and folding fans, who sing.
* '''Taiko-uchi''' (太鼓打ち): Two performers in mon-tsuki, tied with a {{ill|Yaku-himo|ja|奴帯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaku-himo|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, who wear white {{ill|momohiki|ja|股引|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matabiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11611516}} and gaiters, playing drums with sticks.
* '''Sasara-suri''' (ささら摺り): Two performers in {{ill|Kasuri|en|Kasuri|qid=Q3081545|lt=Kasuri}} kimono, wearing short pants, and holding {{ill|Binzasara|en|Binzasara|qid=Q2904003|lt=Binzasara}} (wooden clappers). These roles are played by boys aged 14–15, while all other roles are performed by adult men.
* '''Saotome''' (早乙女): Several performers wearing Edo-style tsumugi kimono and {{ill|Okoso zukin|ja|おこそ頭巾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okoso zukin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} headdresses, carrying small fans and {{ill|yotsutake|ja|四つ竹|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yotsutake|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (four-legged bamboo sticks).

The dance begins with the Kuwagashira's prologue and progresses through themes such as "Seed Planting," "Rice Planting," "Harvesting," "Threshing," "Hulling," "Using the Winnowing Machine," and "Ritual Completion." It concludes with the Kuwagashira delivering a celebratory message.
